Preparation: The soup bone is put over the fire in 6 qts. of cold water after it has been washed in cold water. Soup greens and salt are added and the whole is boiled slowly 4 hours until it is boiled down to 2 or 3 quarts. Before using pour the bouillon through a fine sieve. If you like the bouillon very strong and of a good color add ½ teaspoonful of beef extract.

arxiv-2111-13914.title: Fast and Informative Model Selection using Learning Curve Cross-Validation
arxiv-2111-13914.creator: Felix Mohr, Jan N. van Rijn
arxiv-2111-13914.description: Abstract Common cross-validation (CV) methods like k-fold cross-validation or Monte-Carlo cross-validation estimate the predictive performance of a learner by repeatedly training it on a large portion of the given data and testing on the remaining data. These techniques have two major drawbacks. First, they can be unnecessarily slow on large datasets.

arxiv-2112-02245.title: Proposal for a solid-state magnetoresistive Larmor quantum clock
arxiv-2112-02245.creator: Amal Mathew, Kerem Y Camsari, Bhaskaran Muralidharan
arxiv-2112-02245.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Amal Mathew, Kerem Y Camsari, Bhaskaran Muralidharan. We propose a solid-state implementation of the Larmor clock that exploits tunnel magnetoresistance to distill information on how long itinerant spins take to traverse a barrier embedded in it. Keeping in mind that the tunnelling time innately involves pristine pre-selection and post-selection, our proposal takes into account the detrimental aspects of multiple reflections by incorporating multiple contacts, multiple current measurements and suitably defined magnetoresistance signals.

arxiv-2404-03556.title: Robot Safety Monitoring using Programmable Light Curtains
arxiv-2404-03556.creator: Karnik Ram, Shobhit Aggarwal, Robert Tamburo, Siddharth Ancha, Srinivasa Narasimhan Supplementary website: https://cmu-mfi.github.io/plc-safety/ *
arxiv-2404-03556.description: Abstract As factories continue to evolve into collaborative spaces with multiple robots working together with human supervisors in the loop, ensuring safety for all actors involved becomes critical. Currently, laser-based light curtain sensors are widely used in factories for safety monitoring.

arxiv-2510-03842.title: A Frank-Wolfe Algorithm for Strongly Monotone Variational Inequalities Thanks: The authors are with (1) Delft University of Technology and (2) the University of Toronto. This work was supported by the ERC grant TRUST-949796 and the NSERC Discovery grant RGPIN-2025-06544.
arxiv-2510-03842.creator: Reza Rahimi Baghbadorani 1, Peyman Mohajerin Esfahani 1,2, Sergio Grammatico 1
arxiv-2510-03842.description: Abstract . We propose an accelerated algorithm with a Frank-Wolfe method as an oracle for solving strongly monotone variational inequality problems. While standard solution approaches, such as projected gradient descent (aka value iteration), involve projecting onto the desired set at each iteration, a distinctive feature of our proposed method is the use of a linear minimization oracle in each iteration.

arxiv-2511-17334.title: Simulating Disky Broad Line Region Reverberation
arxiv-2511-17334.creator: Mary Ogborn, Michael Eracleous, Jessie C. Runnoe, Massimo Dotti, Niana N. Mohammed, Collin M. Dabbieri
arxiv-2511-17334.description: Abstract Variability studies of the broad emission lines of Active Galactic Nuclei (AGNs) and quasars show stochastic radial velocity variations (i.e., fluctuations in the centroid of the line), ‘jitter’, on timescales of weeks to months. This jitter may be intrinsic as the broad-line emitting region (BLR) reverberates from the AGN continuum.

pmc-10544019.title: D2O as an Imperfect Replacement for H2O: Problem or Opportunity for Protein Research?
pmc-10544019.creator: Giulia Giubertoni, Mischa Bonn, Sander Woutersen
pmc-10544019.description: D2O is commonly used as a solvent instead of H2O in spectroscopic studies of proteins, in particular, in infrared and nuclear-magnetic-resonance spectroscopy. D2O is chemically equivalent to H2O, and the differences, particularly in hydrogen-bond strength, are often ignored. However, replacing solvent water with D2O can affect not only the kinetics but also the structure and stability of biomolecules.

pmc-11490867.title: Accurate birth weight prediction from fetal biometry using the Gompertz model
pmc-11490867.creator: Chandrani Kumari, Gautam I Menon, Leelavati Narlikar, Uma Ram, Rahul Siddharthan
pmc-11490867.description: ObjectivesMonitoring of fetal growth and estimation of birth weight is of clinical importance. During pregnancy, ultrasound fetal biometry values including femur length, head circumference, abdominal circumference, biparietal diameter are measured and used to place fetuses on “growth charts”. There is no simple growth-model-based, predictive formula in use for fetal biometry.

pmc-11948209.title: Fishing reviewing: A threat to research integrity and credibility
pmc-11948209.creator: Mohammed Al-Beltagi
pmc-11948209.description: The rise of the “fishing reviewer” phenomenon presents a significant threat to the integrity of academic publishing, undermining the credibility of the peer review process and eroding trust in scientific journals. This editorial explores the risk factors contributing to this troubling trend and identifies key indicators to recognize such reviewers.

pmc-12656222.title: Continuous Wireless Vital Sign Sensors for Detecting Severe Deviations at a Transitional Care Facility—An Observational Feasibility Study
pmc-12656222.creator: Jesper Mølgaard, Camilla Haahr-Raunkjaer, Søren Straarup Rasmussen, Loraine Villacorte Andersen, Christian S. Meyhoff, Eske K. Aasvang
pmc-12656222.description: After hospital admissions, patients may be discharged to a transitional care facility if they are considered physically or mentally unable to be at home. This study aimed to assess the feasibility of continuous wearable vital sign monitoring (CVSM) at a low-staffed transitional care facility.

pmc-13081351.title: Adverse events as key risk factors for in-hospital mortality in intensive care units
pmc-13081351.creator: M. Roncal-Redín, D. San Jose-Saras, C. Díaz-Agero Pérez, J. Vicente-Guijarro, P. Moreno-Nunez, B. Peñalver-Argüeso, J. M. Aranaz-Andres, José Lorenzo Valencia Martín, José Lorenzo Valencia Martín, Asunción Colomer Rosas, Inmaculada Mediavilla Herrera, Mª José Esteban Niveiro, Nieves López Fresneña,
pmc-13081351.description: IntroductionIntensive care units (ICUs) represent high-risk environments for adverse events (AEs). Preventing these events requires a solid understanding of their epidemiology based on standardized and validated methodologies. The aim of this study was to quantify AEs using the established Harvard Medical Practice Study (HMPS) methodology, identify associated factors, and analyze their prognostic impact on critically ill patients.

pmc-13567073.creator: Mingliang Guo, Yingying Tang, Tianhao Liu, Zeyuan She, Di Wang, Xianghui Meng, Dagang Tian, Yuan Qin
pmc-13567073.description: Members of the EPIDERMAL PATTERNING FACTOR (EPF) and EPF-Like (EPFL) families perform diverse regulatory functions in plant tissue morphogenesis, controlling the development of stomata, awns, shoot apical meristems (SAMs), and inflorescences. Nevertheless, the biological functions of OsEPF/EPFL family members in mediating responses to biotic/abiotic stresses are not yet widely characterized.

pmc-13581990.title: Neural correlates of information gain during search revealed by fMRI
pmc-13581990.creator: Sakrapee Paisalnan, Yashar Moshfeghi, Frank Pollick
pmc-13581990.description: SummaryWhen confronted with uncertainty, humans engage in information-seeking behavior to gather sufficient information. Identifying the brain regions involved offers insight into the underlying cognitive mechanisms. Using Shannon information theory, we quantified the information contained in the image tiles presented in an fMRI experiment.
